# notata

> Minimal Python library for structured filesystem logging of scientific runs.
> Each run becomes a directory of plain files — parameters, arrays, plots,
> artifacts, metadata and a timestamped log. No server, no database, no
> dashboard. Built for simulations, solvers and parameter sweeps rather than
> machine-learning experiment tracking.

Install with `pip install notata`. Requires Python 3.10+; depends only on
numpy and pyyaml. matplotlib and pandas are optional, used by `Logbook.plot`
and `Experiment.to_dataframe` respectively.

Four public names, all importable from the top-level package:

- `Logbook` — writes one run directory. Context manager marks the run
  `complete` on clean exit, or `failed` with the exception message.
- `Experiment` — parameter sweeps; one run directory per parameter
  combination plus an `index.csv` summary.
- `LogReader` — reads one run directory back.
- `ExperimentReader` — iterates the runs of an experiment.

A run directory is laid out as:

```
log_<run_id>/
  log.txt            [YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS] LEVEL message
  metadata.json      status, start_time, end_time, runtime_sec, failure_reason
  params.yaml        parameter snapshot (params.json if ext="json")
  data/              .npy from array(), .npz from arrays()
  plots/             figures from plot()
  artifacts/         .json, .txt, .pkl, raw bytes
```

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/quickstart.html): first run, in full
- [Directory structure](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/structure.html): what each file holds and its format
- [Naming conventions](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/naming.html): run ids and artifact names
- [API reference](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html): every method, with signatures
- [Experiment sweeps](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/experiment.html): multi-run logging and `index.csv`
- [Reading runs back](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/readers.html): LogReader and ExperimentReader
- [Artifacts](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/artifacts.html): json, text, pickle and raw bytes
- [Plotting](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/plotting.html): saving matplotlib figures
- [Failure handling](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/failures.html): how failed runs are recorded
- [Shell usage](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/shell_usage.html): inspecting runs with grep, cat and friends

## Optional

- [Source](https://github.com/alonfnt/notata): the library is under 900 lines
- [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/notata/): release history
- [Manual lifecycle](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/manual.html): using Logbook without a context manager
- [Manual parameter sweeps](https://notata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/sweeps.html): sweeping with Logbook directly, without Experiment
